text: The Vogel-Fulcher-Tammann law accurately describes critical slowing in bulk polymer glasses, but it lacks an agreed microscopic theory. We derive it from quantum mechanical transition rates, using the logarithm of final-state phase space as the activation entropy. Closed polymer chains are counted as self-avoiding polygons, while open chains anchored to surfaces are treated separately. For uniform connectivity and Flory-type scaling, the resulting activation entropy has the required energy singularity, giving the VFT form. Surface proximity lowers the dynamical singularity temperature, so films only a few nanometers thick no longer strictly obey the empirical bulk law.
